prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1017; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Reviewed the first notice of loss. Insured reports a collision at an intersection while turning left. Other driver's vehicle struck the insured's rear quarter panel. Police report requested. Photos of both vehicles received and saved to file.

Entry 2: Spoke with the claimant by phone. Claimant confirms no attorney is retained and prefers to handle the claim directly. Claimant reports neck strain following the impact and is seeing a primary care provider. Explained the medical documentation needed to evaluate the bodily injury portion of the claim.

Entry 3: Obtained the recorded statement from the insured. Insured states the light had turned green for oncoming traffic and they were waiting for a gap before completing the left turn. Insured believes the other vehicle was approaching at speed. Witness information noted on the police report, to be followed up.

Entry 4: Received the claimant's treatment notes. Diagnosis listed as cervical strain with neck pain and limited range of motion. Treatment plan includes physical therapy sessions and a follow-up visit in four weeks. Medical records added to file for review. Liability still under evaluation pending police report and witness contact.

Entry 5: Sent the claimant a written summary of the coverage position and the next steps, including how to submit receipts for medical expenses and lost time from work. Claimant acknowledged receipt by phone and said they would send the records by the end of the week. File remains open and reserved for bodily injury and property damage.
